title: The Many Names of the One Garment: The Living Soul Dispersed and Gathered
arc: A disciple's question — what do all the various ritual names of the "great garments" actually designate? — leads the Master through an enumeration that shows every name (Jesus, pearl-ornaments, icons-and-tunics, element of light, Cross of Light, Counsel of Life, afflicted soul) as a different facet of one and the same reality: the Living Soul, Divine Truth dispersed throughout the cosmos. The teaching ends by promising that at the consummation all these many names will collapse back into one likeness, one name, in the original substance from which the Living Soul was sent forth against the Enemy.
reading:
This chapter is a catechesis on naming. The disciple, presumably looking at the liturgical and doctrinal vocabulary of the community, asks why so many different terms are used for what is called "the great garments" — Jesus, pearl-ornaments, cluster-pieces, icons, robes-of-work, cross, element of light, crucifix of light, Counsel of Life, the afflicted-slain-strangled-dead soul. Are these different things, or different names for one thing? The answer the Master gives is the latter: all these are names for the Living Soul — Divine Truth dispersed into the natural cosmos — described from different angles of its scattering, suffering, and operation. At the end he draws this back to a single source-substance to which all these multiplied names will eventually return.

The structuring image is the **garment**. In this project's vocabulary, a garment is the external truth in which an interior spiritual reality is clothed; here it is the outer form in which the dispersed Divine Truth is borne in ultimates. The "great garments" are therefore the great vesting-forms in which the Living Soul appears throughout creation. The Master's first identification is the most general: these great garments are the **five noeric ones** — the five-fold completeness of Divine Truth in receptive form — and together they constitute the body of the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man, those chosen in the likeness of the Ambassador. In other words, the whole vocabulary of "great garments" refers to the column of accumulated truth ascending homeward, considered in its dispersed condition before its gathering.

Each subsequent name then names this same reality from one of its operative aspects.

The name "**Jesus, Jesus**" is given to the Power that shines light, that has been swallowed, that produces fruit, that is fashioned in the regions of the cosmos under the upper archons in all the firmaments. This is Divine Truth in its shining-forth as Redeemer — Jesus the Radiance — but here named precisely as the light that is engulfed by the natural and yet still shines and bears fruit there. The "Splendid One" is the same power as it blazes out in the stars of the likeness, manifested through the powers of the Aromos: the same Living Soul considered as it gleams in the particular truths bound in the cosmic circuit. And the "Jesuses" in the lower lands — those fashioned beneath the head of the Omophoros, in the land that he carries — are the same Divine Truth as it is held captive in the lowest natural beneath the divine bearing-up. The Master is saying: wherever the dispersed light is — high in the firmaments, in the stars, or below in the carried earth — it is rightly called "Jesus," because it is one and the same suffering power.

The names "**pearl-ornaments**" and "**cluster-pieces**" identify this same Living Power in its condition as raw material being processed: it is reaped, cut, swallowed, grasped — pluckers gathering it place by place in the five worlds of the flesh. Here the imagery of the pearl (the precious refined truth produced from natural conjunction) is fused with the agricultural imagery of harvest. Both say the same thing: Divine Truth being painfully extracted from the worlds of natural concupiscence.

The names "**icons**" and "**great tunics of work**" point to the **three great garments** — those of wind, of fire, and of water. These are the three elemental media (perception, love, and natural truth) upon which the Living Spirit is mounted, the foundation upon which his works in the worlds rest, the places of "ferrying" by which states are conveyed and scattered before the Omophoros. The Living Soul vested in these three is the cosmic vesture that the Living Spirit himself rides as he carries out the structuring of the natural.

The "**element of light**" is identified as that which stands in everything below and yet is rising upward — gathering inward through the depths of all the lands and casting itself upon them. This is the redemptive countermotion: the same dispersed Divine Truth viewed not in its scattering but in its homeward-streaming. The "**Cross of Light**" is the same Power of Light, but now named in its bound condition — wholly stretched out upon the land, crucified into the natural. The pair "**the Dry one and the Moist one**" appears to continue the same identification under another correspondential pair.

"**The Counsel of Life**" is identified with the Calling and the Hearing — the influx of summoning truth and the soul's responsive reception — that which fills all the powers, awakens them, gives them breadth, and embraces them so that they may be filled. The Living Soul in its rational-disposing aspect is therefore the very mechanism of the Call-and-Hearing by which the captive light is roused.

Finally "**the soul that is afflicted, slain, troubled, dead**" — the most concretely sorrowful name — is identified with the power of the fruits and seeds of every kind, the food-reality that is crushed, broken, pounded, and given as nourishment to the worlds of the flesh; and likewise with the herbage that is torn up and dried. This is the most ultimate face of the Living Soul: Divine Truth suffering its passion in the very produce of the earth, undergoing slaughter every day in eating and harvesting. The Master notes that this slain quality belongs to her entire kind — wherever she is taken, she is slain there.

The closing movement is the doctrinal heart of the teaching. After all these names have been enumerated, the Master says: their **origin is one from the beginning**, and one substance shines through them all. They were divided into all these many kinds **in the first contest** — that is, in the primordial battle when Divine Truth was sent forth against the Enemy and was scattered to overcome him. They stood firm in altered likenesses and acquired many names because of the many forms the contest required. But this multiplication of names is provisional. When all these forms shall be broken apart, when the dispersed light is **stripped naked of all the figures** and the names **separated forth**, then everything they named shall be **gathered inward** into one likeness, one name, unchanging and unmoving forever, in the region of its first substance — the very region from which it was originally sent forth against the Enemy.

The teaching, therefore, is doing two things at once. First, it is teaching that the apparent multiplicity of cosmological-liturgical names — Jesus, pearl, icon, tunic, cross, element, counsel, suffering soul — is not a multiplicity of objects but a multiplicity of correspondential aspects of one reality, the Living Soul / Divine Truth dispersed in the natural. Second, it is teaching the eschatological law that this multiplication itself is a feature of the mingled state, and that regeneration's culmination is the unmaking of the multiplicity: every garment will be put off, every figure stripped, every name gathered into one name, when the light returns to its first substance. The garments were necessary for the war; in the peace they fall away, and the one Divine Truth stands again uniform in its source.
